newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of GDP.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were steady on Wednesday in moderate trade, dealers said.

Most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the first-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data, which is forecast to show a 4.1 percent annual growth rate compared with 3.8 percent growth in the fourth-quarter of 1996, they said.

The American Production and Inventory Control (APICS) survey, New York National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index and Chicago Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) figures due later tonight will probably be non-events, they added.
"Rates were narrowly mixed in the morning on some sporadic position adjustments. Basically, everyone is waiting for fresh direction from tonight's GDP, APICS, NAPM and PMI data," a local dealer said.

"There won't be much impact as the main focus will be on the GDP numbers and the market will be closed tomorrow for the May Day holiday. But some people are waiting for possible direction from this Friday's employment report," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent but Thursday/Friday eased 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.
Week-fixed was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent and three-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent. Nine-months eased 1/16 point to 6-3/16 6-1/16 percent and twelve-months eased 1/8 point to 6-5/16 6-3/16 percent.
